title.narrative: Support to TAHA: Growing Wealth Through Horticulture (GROWTH)
Support to TAHA: Growing Wealth Through Horticulture (GROWTH)

description.narrative:
The contribution aims to contribute to increased commercial competitiveness and sustainability of the horticultural sector in Tanzania. The Swedish support is directed to the non-profit Association (TAHA) through the project 'Growing Wealth through Horticulture'. The focus is to increase knowledge on sustainable and climate resilient farming methods and increases economic gains through improved marketing and trade facilitation.
Using market systems development approach, the project works with actors at all levels of the horticulture value chain, namely: input suppliers, producers, processors, logistics service providers, traders, and consumers. In addition, the project work with value chain supporting institutions such as finance, quality and standards accreditation institutions and providers of entrepreneurship services. A range of demand-driven horticultural crops are currently grown and can be cultivated in the various agro-ecological zones/regions. TAHA is therefore continuing to establish tailored information systems to link producers on supply side and the demand side with the required standards for a diverse range of horticultural products in the domestic, East African region, Southern Africa, Europe and Middle Eastern areas.
Analysis and advocacy for better policy and business regulatory environment is an important pillar of the intervention to attract investment and trade. The outcome results of the project includes increased opportunities for jobs and incomes at micro level and increase in sector's contribution to economic growth. The expected impact of the the intervention is the contribution of the sector in alleviation of income /resource and other dimensions of Poverty. The project also contribute to creating awareness on improved nutrition and gender integration

Projektets övergripande mål är att öka konkurrenskraft och hållbarhet för hortikultur (trädgårdsodling). Det svenska stödet riktas till den ideella organisationen (TAHA) genom projektet "Growing Wealth through Horticulture" med fokus på: • Öka produktiviteten genom att förbättra kunskap om effektiva och hållbara jordbruksmetoder, med tonvikt på att integrera miljö och klimatförändringar, • Öka tillgången till marknader för tanzaniska hortikultur produkter, • Bidra till opinionsbildning och främjande av en bättre politik och affärsmöjliggörande miljö för hortikulturens konkurrenskraft och delaktighet.

The overall objective (s) of the Project is increasing competitiveness and sustainability of horticultural industry. The Swedish support is directed to the non-profit Association (TAHA) through the project "Growing Wealth through Horticulture" with focus on: • Increasing productivity by improved knowledge on efficient and sustainable farming methods, with emphasis on integrating environment and climate change , • increase access to markets for Tanzanian horticultural products, • Contributing to advocacy for better policy and business enabling environment for horticultural industry's competitiveness and inclusiveness.

Support to TAHA: Growing Wealth Through Horticulture (GROWTH)

description.narrative:
Regarding increasing productivity, there has been a satisfactory result in building capacity on sustainable farming methods. A good number (159, 000) farmers have been trained on sustainable horticultural farming practices which includes environmentally friendly and climate smart agricultural practices which have resulted in increase of productivity for vegetables, fruits and spices of between 20 to 50 percent. For instance, avocado, as an emerging value chain of interest to famers in Tanzania, the production has been increasing at an incredible pace and it might overtake Kenya, the regional leader in coming two or three years. The export of Tanzania horticulture crops by TAHA accredited off-takers including avocadoes is also increasing.
Regarding the Access to Markets, TAHA continues to facilitate trading of horticultural products to local, regional (especially East Africa) and international (notably European markets). The facilitation includes cargo logistics and handling and ensuring farmers compliance with food safety and other certification standards. TAHAs also works to build capacity on pesticides use and avoid environmental and health hazardous pesticides, herbicides and other agrochemicals. TAHA role is to ensure producers are trained well and facilities the audit on certification standards.
It is reported that close to 107,000 farmers sold about 228,000 metric tons of selected horticultural crops earning about $160 million dollars. Avocado has emerged as a prominent value chain product exported from Tanzania. However, due to the Red Sea piracy crisis TAHA anticipates either a decrease in export volume to European markets or less income fetched because of the high cost charged by vessels or both, as a result using airfreight or longer sea route via The Cape of Good of Hope
Because the contribution includes the result with environment marker, promoting tree crops were assessed one of the immediate outputs to achieve this objective. Trees crops such as fruit or spices trees provide duo benefits: economic benefits (food and income) and reforestation. It is reported that four (4) new seedlings nurseries for avocado, cloves, cardamon, cinnamon and trees were established in Tanga, Arusha and Kilimanjaro. Moreover, more than 17,000 farmers were trained physically on Good Agricultural Practices, the environmental Smart Horticulture techniques to mitigate adverse effects caused by climate change.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
